content.title: Michigan vs Saint Louis highlights: Wolverines beat Billikens to advance to Sweet 16
content.text: Updated March 21, 2026, 4:17 p.m. ETFollow all of Saturday's NCAA Tournament second round games with USA TODAY Sports' live updates.Michigan basketball is heading to the Sweet 16.The No. 1-seeded Wolverines pulled away from No. 9 Saint Louis in the second half to earn a 95-72 win on Saturday, March 21. Michigan will play the winner of No. 4 Alabama and No. 5 Texas Tech next Friday, March 27.Yaxel Lendeborg was explosive in the second half for the Wolverines, scoring 14 of his game-high 25 points. He shot 9-of-13 from the field and added six rebounds. Aday Mara added 16 points, five rebounds, five assists and four blocks. Elliot Cadeau had 12 points and eight assists.Michigan led by nine points at halftime before outscoring the Billikens 47-33 in the second half for the victory.Amari McCottry led Saint Louis with 14 points, while Dion Brown added 13 points. The key to victory for Michigan was holding Robbie Avila to nine points on 3-for-13 shooting, including 3-for-10 shooting from 3-point range. Avila entered the game 19 points shy of 2,000 points for his career.USA TODAY brought you live updates from the 2026 NCAA Tournament second-round matchup between Saint Louis and Michigan. Michigan seven minutes away from Sweet 16Michigan is about seven minutes away from a Sweet 16 appearance, holding an 81-63 lead over Saint Louis with 7:17 remaining in the game. Yaxel Lendeborg is up to 20 points, including nine in the second half.The Billikens have shot 47% for the game, but the Wolverines are shooting even better at 57%. Michigan pulling away from Saint LouisA 7-0 run by Michigan has it leading by a game-high 15 points at 73-58 with 10:30 left in the game. Yaxel Lendeborg has taken over in the second half with seven of his game-high 18 points coming in the half. Michigan leads by 9 pointsMichigan pushes its lead back to nine points at 66-57 with 11:44 left in the game. Saint Louis had a couple of opportunities to cut the game to a one-score contest, but could not convert. Saint Louis sticking aroundSaint Louis keeps absorbing blows from Michigan, but is sticking around. The Wolverines lead 61-55 at the first media timeout with 14:17 left in the game.The Billikens have outscored Michigan 16-13 in the second half. Robbie Avila is up to nine points after hitting a pair of 3-pointers in this half.
